narrative:
# DRAM controller measurements
 The first comparison sets the tree before the DRAM controller work (commit `041c09a`) against the tree that adds the DDR passive trip (commit `13037cf`), using the budgets in the [DRAM controller design](dram-controller.md). Neither tree has code for the memory-bus priority hook, the display-port latency window or the copy load, so their rows in that comparison record no measurement. The [second comparison](#memory-bus-priority-window-and-decode-check) measures that code against the budgets of the [memory-bus priority design](dram-bus-priority.md).
 ## Conditions

- **Builds.** Both trees were built with the project's aarch64 Clang toolchain
  in separate directories under
  `~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/dram-controller-measure/`: the thermal image
  (`SUNSTONE_A733_THERMAL=ON`), the monitor image (`SUNSTONE_A733_MONITOR=ON`)
  and the integrated OS image (`SUNSTONE_A733_OS=ON`). These are the three
  images that link `drivers/thermal/a733_thermal.c`.
- **Sizes.** `llvm-size` and `llvm-nm` on the driver object and on each linked
  image.
- **Instruction counts.** `policy_emu.py` in the same directory loads each
  linked thermal and OS image into Unicorn 2.1.4, initializes a policy, and
  calls the linked `a733_thermal_policy_update` with one five-channel sample
  every 250 ms. Each count covers one call, including the two instructions of
  the stub that stands in for the notification callback. The script also
  counts `DSB`, `DMB` and `ISB` instructions and acquire or release accesses.
- **Host check.** `checks/thermal-policy.c` was compiled with
  AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer against each tree's driver.
- No board was used.
 ## Results

| Metric | Budget | Before | After | Within budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hook accesses | 2 CCU reads; at most 27 NSI accesses; 1 lock pair | 0 | 0; no hook code exists | Not measurable |
| Added accesses, tasks, timers and interrupts in HDMI, DisplayPort and steady-state images | 0 | 0 | 0 | Yes |
| Window accesses and barriers per phase | Start 6 NSI accesses, 2 ISB; collect 6 NSI reads, 1 ISB; no added DSB | None | None; no window code exists | Not measurable |
| Counter headroom over a 50 ms period | No 32-bit wrap | Not applicable | Arithmetic holds | Yes |
| Copy-load stop | No pass after the end phase | Not applicable | No copy-load code exists | Not measurable |
| Scan-out latency | Board result | Not measured | Not measured | Not measurable on the host |
| DDR trip, behavior | THROTTLE at 85.019 °C, held to 83.013 °C, released at 82.954 °C | No passive trip | As budgeted | Yes |
| DDR trip, instructions per policy update | Not budgeted | 196 | 199 to 217 | See below |
| DDR trip, notifications | 1 per level change | 0 | 1 at the trip, 1 at release, 0 otherwise | Yes |
| DDR trip, barriers per policy update | No added barrier | 0 | 0 | Yes |
| DDR trip, recognition real-time factor | At most 1.05 times the value without the trip | Not measured | Not measured | Board measurement |
| Code size outside the load mode | At most 2 KiB text, 128 B data | 0 | 68 B text, 0 B data | Yes |
 ### DDR trip
 The policy update in the linked images takes these instruction counts per call. The thermal image and the OS image give identical counts.

| Sample | Before | After | Level after the call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All channels at 30.008 °C | 196 | 207 | NORMAL |
| DDR at 84.960 °C | 196 | 203 | NORMAL |
| DDR at 85.019 °C | 196 | 209, one notification | THROTTLE |
| DDR at 84.960 °C, then 83.013 °C | 196 | 199 | THROTTLE |
| DDR at 82.954 °C | 196 | 217, one notification | NORMAL |
| All channels at 30.008 °C after release | 196 | 207 | NORMAL |
 Before the change, the compiler omitted the passive comparison for the DDR channel because its table entry was zero. The steady-state update therefore costs 11 more instructions, a 5.6% increase. That cost is the 85 °C comparison and its hysteresis test, which the design requires because LPDDR5 standard refresh is specified only up to 85 °C. The update runs once per THS sample, has no barrier and touches no register, so the added cost is a few nanoseconds per sample. Each call makes one release store in steady state and two when the level changes, in both trees.
 The policy check passes against both trees. The new check fails against the old driver at its first DDR case, which shows that the check covers the trip.
 ### Code size

- `a733_thermal.c` text grows from 10,408 to 10,476 bytes. All 68 bytes are
  in `a733_thermal_policy_update` (1,216 to 1,284 bytes). The trip table is
  folded into the code, so no data or read-only data is added.
- Thermal image text grows from 512,732 to 512,800 bytes.
- OS image text grows from 843,680 to 843,744 bytes. The only symbol whose
  size changes is `a733_thermal_policy_update`.
- Monitor image text, read-only data and data sizes are unchanged. Its
  loadable bytes differ only in the 32-byte `a733_smp_build_id`, a digest of
  the build inputs, which include the changed `a733_thermal.h`. The monitor
  links no policy code.
 ### Counter headroom
 At the 76.8 GB/s peak, a 50 ms period moves 3.84 GB, which is 2.4 × 10⁸ port 2 data units of 16 bytes. The period register holds 3 × 10⁷ cycles at a
600 MHz MBUS clock. Both are below 2³² (4.29 × 10⁹). By Little's law, the read latency sum over one period equals the mean number of outstanding reads times 3 × 10⁷ cycles, so it stays below 2³² while DE averages fewer than 143 outstanding reads. These figures match the design.

## Measurement
 `apps/gpu-display/dram-controller-load.c`, compiled only with `SUNSTONE_GPU_DISPLAY_DRAM_LOAD=ON`, produces the windows. The table and no-table load images run in one board session.

- **Session.** After the third presentation, slot 0 scans out 1280×720 RGB565
  at 60 Hz (110.6 MB/s). Phase A lasts 2 s (40 windows) with scan-out only.
  Phase B adds the copy load until `stop_at` − 1 s and needs at least 8 s (160
  windows). `stop_at` is 18 s into the 20 s session, so the third presentation
  must come by 7 s. The host model places it at 0.27 s, and the presentation
  record's `observed_us` gives the board time. A later presentation makes the
  run inconclusive.
- **Copy load.** `a733_smp_diagnostic_start` creates eight tasks with
  `xTaskCreateStaticAffinitySet`, priority 1, a NULL context and affinity mask
  `1 << core` for cores 0–7. `gpu_display_task_privileged` admits their entry
  with a NULL context in the load build only, so they run at EL1. Each task
  takes its slot from `portGET_CORE_ID()`. Before creating them,
  `a733_smp_diagnostic_start` acquires one 32 MiB lease at 2 MiB alignment
  from the write-back pool (`a733_memory_reservations_init`, 768 MiB) under
  owner `GPU_DISPLAY_DRAM_LOAD_OWNER`, a value no other gpu-display owner uses.
  The lease stays in `DEVICE_MEMORY_CPU` until power-off and no device is
  granted it. Each task copies between a 2 MiB source and a 2 MiB destination
  with a loop of two `LDP` and two `STP` of Q registers. Every task already
  saves Q0–Q31 (`configUSE_TASK_FPU_SUPPORT` is 2).
- **Inherited fields.** Nothing in the OS resets the NSI or restores the port
  fields, so a table written earlier in a board session persists. The session
  therefore runs the no-table load image before any image that writes the
  table. A no-table run counts only if its recorded inherited fields of ports
  2, 14 and 15 differ from the table. If boot0 already sets the table values,
  the scan-out row is recorded as not demonstrable.
  `capture.py` enforces the field rule when it moves to reply version 2.
- **Conclusiveness.** The no-table image must show contention: its phase B mean
  latency must exceed its phase A mean by more than 2 √(SE_A² + SE_B²). If it
  does not, the next load image raises the clusters through the existing CPU
  clock driver. If that run still shows no contention, the scan-out row is
  recorded as not demonstrable under CPU load and the table stays at the vendor
  values. CPU bandwidth per core is passes × 4 MiB over the phase B time. A
  run whose phase B was abandoned is inconclusive.
- **Latency statistic.** For each accepted window, x is port 2's latency sum
  divided by its read requests, in MBUS cycles per request, Q8 fixed point. A
  window with x ≥ 2²⁴ counts as out of range, so Σx² over at most 360 windows
  stays below 2⁵⁷. Per phase the block holds Σx and Σx². The host tool derives
  the mean m, the standard deviation and the standard error SE over the n
  accepted windows.
- **Transport.** The gpu-display observation reply's `terminal.reserved[136]`,
  bytes 888..1023, becomes the evidence block and the reply version becomes 2.
  The 1,024-byte size and its static assert stay. `capture.py` accepts only
  reply version 2 from gpu-display. The hook writes the block directly: it
  zeroes it and fills the hook fields, with result bits from the build macro
  and its own result. `a733_dram_window_block()` in the load object adds the
  window and copy-slot fields, so images without the load mode link no
  packing code for them.

  | Offset | Fields |
  | --- | --- |
  | 0 | `u16` ×8: windows started, accepted in phase A, accepted in phase B, refused late, refused idle, refused free-running, out of range, abandoned |
  | 16 | `u16`: result bits (hook built, table image, hook result, collect disables first, phases ended early, `MBUS_DFS_EN` found set); `u16`: stopping field of a failed hook (0, 1 + 3 × port index + field index, or 10 for a failed CCU read) |
  | 20 | `u16` ×6: inherited and final fields of ports 2, 14 and 15 (mode bits 1–0, priority bits 5–2, select bit 6) |
  | 32 | `u16` ×4: configured CPU-L, CPU-B and DSU MHz (0 when undecoded); at offset 38, `phase_ticks_max`, the longest start or collect in 24 MHz counter ticks, saturating at 65,535 |
  | 40 | `u32` ×2: CCU `+0x580`, `+0x584` |
  | 48 | `u32` ×2: `fabric_hz[2]`; phase B length in ms |
  | 56 | `u64` ×6: per phase, Σx, Σx², port 2 read data |
  | 104 | `u32` ×8: copy passes per core in phase B |

Budget rows for the board: ## Performance budgets
 Access counts come from host models that run the compiled code against counting register files. Times come from the architectural counter on the board.

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hook | 2 CCU reads; per field 1 NSI access at target, else 3; at most 27 NSI accesses; 1 lock pair; once per framebuffer instance; 0 NSI accesses when the NSI is not running | Host model of the framebuffer prepare sequence | 0 OS accesses |
| HDMI, DisplayPort and steady state | 0 added accesses, tasks, timers or interrupts | Linked-symbol check; host model | 0 |
| Window | Init: 8 clock reads, once. Start: 6 NSI accesses (the first start of a session also reads `+0x588`), 1 lock pair, 2 ISB, no added DSB. Collect: 6 NSI reads (7 accesses after the fallback), 1 lock pair, 1 ISB, no added DSB. Abandon: 0 register accesses; 1 counter read in phase B. Pending: 1 ISB, 1 counter read. At most 20 µs per phase | Host model per phase; `phase_ticks_max` on the board | None |
| Counter headroom | No 32-bit wrap in P | Arithmetic at 76.8 GB/s: port 2 ≤ 2.4 × 10⁸ units; period ≤ 3 × 10⁷ cycles at 600 MHz; latency sum below 2³² while DE averages under 143 reads outstanding | Not applicable |
| Copy-load stop | No pass starts after the end phase or a state change is stored | Host model of the copy task loop | Not applicable |
| Scan-out | HDMI stays `ACTIVE` without `A733_HDMI_UNDERFLOW`; m(no table) − m(table) in phase B > 2 √(SE₁² + SE₂²) | Both load images, under the conclusiveness rule | Not measured |
| DDR trip | RTF ≤ 1.05 × without the trip; DDR ≥ 85 °C while CPUB < 90 °C for at most 60 s of 600 s | OS image recognizing recorded input for 10 min, 25 °C ambient, fan off, with and without the trip; also time at the 1014 MHz cap | Not measured: RTF, DDR − CPUB per sample, time each channel is ≥ 85 °C. Both runs belong in the board session that qualifies the throttle, before THROTTLE reaches the CPU clock driver |
| Code size | ≤ 2 KiB text, ≤ 128 B data outside the load mode | `llvm-size` | 0 |
 RTF is recognition wall time divided by audio duration. If a conclusive run fails the scan-out row, the table and the hook are removed. The DDR trip stays even past its bound, because refresh behavior above 85 °C is unknown. The trip is raised only when boot0's derated-refresh setting or MR4-driven refresh is shown.
conclusion: Not yet run. No image links the hook, the window or the copy load, and apps/gpu-display/dram-controller-load.c, the framebuffer edits and the observation reply version 2 do not exist in the tree. The scan-out, CPU time per phase and DDR real-time-factor rows are open.

Board evidence that would confirm the design: ## Board evidence that would confirm the design

- Inherited fields and the two CCU words from the no-table load image, the
  first image that accesses the NSI, then final fields from the table load
  image. The normal gpu-display image gains the hook only after both.
- The scan-out row from both load images, no-table image first, with the
  inherited fields, the CPU clocks, the copy passes per core, the third
  presentation time and the collect order bit, which shows whether the
  counters hold or run past the period.
- The DDR trip row with its baseline and capped-interval figures.
- The offset between the THS DDR channel and the DRAM die: a thermocouple on
  the LPDDR5 package read alongside the channel during the DDR trip run.

Integration edits and host cases that the board run needs: ## Changes outside this component
 No package in this wave owns `drivers/display/a733_display_framebuffer.c` or its header, or `cmake/a733-gpu-display.cmake`. The coordinator assigns those edits, and the hook and window code merge with them. The gpu-graphics package owns `apps/gpu-display/` and `checks/gpu-display*`, and the memory-architecture package owns `checks/device-memory-*`. The `checks/thermal-policy.c` edit merges with the DDR trip, because the trip breaks its old DDR case.

- Framebuffer: `dram_address()`, the stage 4 call and the evidence member
  under `SUNSTONE_DRAM_PRIORITY`, and the load accessor under
  `SUNSTONE_GPU_DISPLAY_DRAM_LOAD`.
- `apps/gpu-display`: the evidence block and reply version 2 in
  `observation.h`. In the load build only, the window step and abandon rules in
  `display.c`, the copy tasks, lease and privileged entry in `main.c`, and the
  owner constant in `application.h`. `capture.py` and the observation host
  cases move to reply version 2.
- `cmake/a733-gpu-display.cmake`: the two flags for the three images.
- `checks/device-memory-capacity.c`: a replay that acquires the load image's
  write-back leases, including the 32 MiB lease at 2 MiB alignment.
- `checks/thermal-policy.c` changes with the DDR trip. Its DDR reading in the
  case without a passive trip is code 1395 (84.96 °C), and its
  single-channel critical case uses the NPU channel. New cases expect
  THROTTLE at code 1394 (85.02 °C), hold it at 1428 (83.01 °C), release it at
  1429 (82.95 °C) and reach CRITICAL at 970 while throttled.
- `checks/index.json`: `checks/dram-controller.py` enters the index in the
  same merge as the hook.
 New host cases in `checks/dram-*`. The cases that need the framebuffer and gpu-display edits are a merge condition for the change that first links `a733_dram.c` or `a733_dram_load.c` into an image, and the hook is not recorded as tested before they pass:

- a full prepare sequence with `+0x580` bit 31 clear makes zero NSI accesses;
  with only reset bit 30 or a `+0x584` bit wrong, it reaches the stage 4
  failure path with zero NSI accesses;
- a full prepare sequence calls the hook once, at the step from stage 4 to 5;
- a mismatch at each port and field reaches the failure path and leaves later
  fields untouched; unrelated bits survive every write; a difference outside
  the mask is not a mismatch; priority subfields 3 and 1 with p = 3 become
  `0xf`;
- the reads-only build writes nothing; an HDMI build makes no NSI access;
- the period written is P × `fabric_hz[2]`; a start at stage 4, in state 2 or
  3 or after phase B makes zero accesses;
- each refusal rule, including zero read requests, refuses as specified;
  collect makes no write before the fallback and one after the first
  free-running refusal, including one refusal among held windows;
- a first start with `+0x588` bit 28 set makes that one read and no port
  access, and ends the phases early;
- abandon at `stop_at` and at `output_fault` makes zero register accesses;
  an abandon in phase B records the phase B end and the early-end bit;
- no copy pass starts after the end phase or state 3 is stored.
